title: The Little World's Fair
teaser: Opening day is here, and your puppy is the guest of honor.
clue: A brand-new fair is opening in your living room, and there is only one guest on the list.
reveal: Four tiny pavilions, each with its own feel underfoot and its own little prize. Your puppy chooses the order, and your puppy decides when the fair closes.
objective: Open a pocket-size fair at home where a young puppy visits stations of safe, gentle textures and finds a small prize at each.
instructions: Build four pavilions on the floor in one room, each about the size of a dinner tray: a folded fleece (Fluff), a flat sheet of paper (Crinkle), a smooth tile or baking tray (Cool), and a firm folded duvet (Squish). Keep every one low and stable.
Hide a prize at each pavilion's center: two or three pieces of your puppy's usual food, or a favorite soft toy. Cover it loosely with a corner of the surface so a nose has to do the finding.
Make a paper 'passport' with four empty boxes. Put it on your lap and sit on the floor away from the pavilions. The fair opens when your puppy walks over.
Say nothing and let your puppy pick the order. Each time they step on a pavilion or sniff out its prize, stamp one box with a pen or a stamp pad (on the paper, never on your puppy).
Skipped pavilions are fine. If a surface worries them, slide it away and leave the prize beside it. Nothing is carried over or coaxed.
When your puppy wanders off, flops or finds a nap, the fair is closed. Pack up the pavilions you used and leave the unvisited ones for tomorrow.
twist: Nothing is judged: your puppy is the only visitor, every stamp is earned by their own paws and nose, and a prize is waiting under each surface.
variations: No food: hide a favorite soft toy or a cloth that smells of home as the prize.
Two pavilions only for very young or very sleepy puppies, then a nap.
Add a 'Rumble' pavilion later: a lightweight towel-wrapped cardboard tube lying flat.
Seated owner: put the pavilions in a row within arm's reach of your chair.
completion: Your puppy has visited at least one pavilion and found its prize. Any number of stamps counts.
photoIdea: The finished fair from floor level with the passport beside it, or the puppy in mid-sniff on a pavilion.
memoryPrompt: Which pavilion did your puppy pick first, and which surprised you?
substitutes: No tile? A cool, clean baking tray.
dietNotes: Use only a few pieces of your puppy's usual food from the day's ration, or skip food and use a toy. Ask your vet about puppy diet.
safety: Home only: keep your puppy indoors until your vet says public places are fine, and ask about vaccinations.
Paper is for stepping on, not chewing. Take away anything your teething puppy shreds or mouths.
Keep it short, offer rest, and never place or coax your puppy onto a surface.
